summary: Méribel Altiport (MFX) is a high-altitude mountain airstrip serving the world-renowned Méribel ski resort in the French Alps, part of the vast Trois Vallées ski domain. The airport sits at approximately 1,700 meters elevation in the commune of Les Allues and is prized for its dramatic mountain approach. It operates primarily during the winter ski season, accommodating private aircraft and small charter flights carrying passengers directly to one of Europe's most prestigious ski destinations.
faqs:
Q: What is an altiport?
A: An altiport is a small airport situated at high altitude, typically in mountainous terrain, designed to serve remote Alpine communities and ski resorts. Méribel Altiport requires specially trained pilots due to its challenging mountain approach.

Q: When is Méribel Altiport open?
A: The altiport operates mainly during the winter ski season, generally from December through April. It may have limited or no operations outside the ski season due to snow conditions and demand.

Q: What types of aircraft can use Méribel Altiport?
A: The altiport handles small private aircraft, turboprops, business jets, and helicopters. Its short runway and mountain location limit the size of aircraft that can safely operate there.

Q: Is Méribel Altiport suitable for commercial airlines?
A: No, Méribel Altiport does not serve scheduled commercial airlines. Travelers flying commercially typically use larger airports like Geneva, Chambéry, or Lyon, then transfer by ground transport or helicopter to Méribel.
transport_tips: Passengers arriving at Méribel Altiport can arrange pre-booked transfers or taxis to reach ski chalets and hotels within the resort, typically a short drive away. During peak ski season, demand for ground transport is high, so advance reservations are strongly recommended. Many visitors also use helicopter transfer services from larger regional airports like Geneva or Chambéry directly to Méribel for greater convenience.
local_tip: Request a mountain-side landing approach when booking your flight if conditions allow—sitting on the right side of smaller aircraft often provides spectacular views of the snow-capped peaks surrounding the Trois Vallées during descent into Méribel.
